task_summary: Fixed Docker Compose ngrok tunnel setup: resolved external network naming mismatch ('cms-v2_cms_network'), isolated compose project ('cms-v2-tunnel') to prevent core stack orphan warnings, fixed token clobbering by loading .env/.env.deploy/.env.prod, removed deprecated bind_tls, copied ngrok.yml into Dockerfile with web_addr 0.0.0.0:4040, added domain sanitization and --log=stdout.
root_causes_identified: External network name mismatch: 'networks.cms_network' was declared with 'external: true' without an explicit name, causing Docker Compose to look for 'cms_network' instead of the active 'cms-v2_cms_network' created by docker-compose.yml.

Project name collision: Without an explicit project name, docker-compose.ngrok.yml defaulted to 'cms-v2' and flagged all running core containers (client, server, mongodb, redis, minio, ollama, etc.) as orphan containers.
Environment variable clobbering: 'NGROK_AUTHTOKEN: ${NGROK_AUTHTOKEN:-}' in the environment block clobbered tokens from .env.deploy/.env.prod with empty string if not exported in host shell.

Web inspector binding refusal: Ngrok defaulted web inspection to 127.0.0.1:4040 inside container; binding web_addr: 0.0.0.0:4040 and copying ngrok.yml into image enables access via http://localhost:4040.
Deprecated config field: Ngrok v3 rejected 'bind_tls: true' in docker/ngrok.yml during config check.
Silent logs in detached mode: Without --log=stdout, ngrok did not output tunnel connection details to docker logs.

verification_evidence.ngrok_tunnels_api_response: 200 OK with public tunnel active and inspector healthy
